subject: history_social
passage: Historians once traced the spread of papermaking from China to the Islamic world to a single dramatic episode. According to this account, Chinese prisoners captured at the Battle of Talas in 751 taught the craft to their captors in Samarkand, from which it soon reached Baghdad and, centuries later, Europe. Many scholars now regard the story with skepticism, observing that it appears only in sources written long after the battle and that paper seems to have been known in Central Asia well before 751. ______ they propose that the technique traveled westward gradually, carried along trade routes by merchants and artisans over generations rather than introduced in a single stroke.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

explanation.why: The third sentence says scholars doubt the single-episode story. The last sentence gives the account these scholars put in its place: a gradual spread along trade routes. The transition must introduce an alternative to an idea just rejected.
explanation.A: Correct. "Instead" signals that the gradual-spread account replaces the doubted single-episode story.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The gradual-spread account is not an example of the scholars' skepticism; it is their alternative explanation.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Nevertheless" would mean scholars propose a gradual spread in spite of their skepticism, but their skepticism is exactly what leads them to the new account. This is the closest near miss.
explanation.D: Incorrect. "Likewise" signals a similar point, but the new account differs from the old story rather than resembling it.
